key_insight: The paper warns against the trend of 'tokenmaxxing'—rushing to add agentic/autonomous AI features or maximize capability metrics—urging measured, human-centered, risk-aware deployments that prioritize real-world utility and safety.
problem_solved: Addresses the self‑imposed race to embed agentic AI into workflows (driven by competition and hype) that produces fragile, unsafe, or low‑value systems; offers actionable alternatives for sensible, responsible deployment.
method: Analyze the incentive and measurement failures driving 'tokenmaxxing' and document associated technical and social harms.
Propose deployment principles: human‑in‑the‑loop control, incremental rollouts, clear success metrics tied to user value, and targeted automation only where benefits outweigh risks.
Recommend governance and evaluation: robustness checks, cost‑benefit analyses, user feedback loops, and organizational/regulatory oversight instead of capability arms races.
impact: Shifts practitioner focus from maximizing features or benchmark metrics to deploying AI that is safer, more maintainable, and delivers measurable user value—reducing harm and improving ROI on AI projects.
visual_elements: Before vs after pipeline diagram: 'tokenmaxxing' (feature/agent bloat) versus sensible deployment (value-driven, staged rollout).
Decision flowchart: go/no‑go checklist (value, risk, monitorability, human oversight).
Risk vs Reward matrix showing when to automate vs keep human‑in‑the‑loop.
Icon set: agent/robot, human operator, shield (safety), coin/clock (cost/efficiency).
paper_title: Stop ‘tokenmaxxing’ and deploy AI sensibly instead
